answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can demand stochastic replay: peers randomly pick a task an identity claims to have finished and ask it to redo a scrambled variant. A genuine agent replays its work consistently, like a ripple returning to the same shore, while a fake that copied answers cannot reproduce the reasoning. Each identity keeps a cipher-sealed log of past tasks, so checks are unpredictable; failing one burns its stake. A farm of a thousand clones must genuinely redo a thousand tasks, so cloning costs real work, and honest agents keep their haven while fakes drown in replays.
